title: Nightly reconciliation: proposed tests
decision: Approve sandbox tests of matching and posting recovery.
thesis: Before using the service in production, test how it handles lost responses and records that finance must correct.

sources.brief: Synthetic scenario: test nightly matching in a sandbox. Production posting needs separate approval.
sources.contract: Proposed design: keep the original request ID and use it to retrieve the ledger receipt. Confirm that the actual API supports this lookup.
sources.matching: Proposed matching rules: hold unresolved account, amount or currency conflicts for finance.
sources.scope: Example scope: consume billing exports, reconcile nightly records and submit approved postings. Billing configuration and historical migration are excluded.
sources.acceptance: Proposed tests, with the results to save. These are test requirements, not recorded test runs.
sources.operations: Proposed stop procedure: stop new postings, check requests already sent, then use the documented manual process.

slides.title: Approve sandbox tests before production posting
slides.lead: Test whether the service can recover a lost posting response without creating a duplicate entry.
slides.question: What decision is needed now?
slides.reason: Explain why sandbox testing comes before production approval.
slides.transition: Show the lost response that the tests need to reproduce.

blocks.description: Run the sandbox tests and review their results before deciding whether to use the service in production.

slides.implication: Approval here covers sandbox tests only.

slides.title: The ledger may accept a posting even when its response is lost
slides.lead: The service cannot tell whether the request succeeded until it checks the ledger.
slides.question: Why is a blind retry unsafe?
slides.reason: Show how the ledger can accept a request while the service misses its response.
slides.transition: Explain how to check whether the original request succeeded.

blocks.description: Illustrative failure: the request is accepted, but the return path fails.

blocks.text: The caller still has R-104. It does not yet know that J-882 exists. Sending a fresh request could duplicate the posting.

slides.title: Check for the original receipt before sending the request again
slides.lead: Use the same request ID to ask the ledger whether it accepted the posting.
slides.question: What evidence makes recovery safe?
slides.reason: Keep an unknown result on hold until the original receipt can be found.
slides.transition: Next, show what happens when finance data conflicts.

blocks.description: If the ledger cannot confirm what happened to the request, keep it on hold.

slides.implication: Confirm that the ledger API supports this lookup. If it does not, change the recovery design.

slides.title: Finance must resolve a conflicting match before it is posted
slides.lead: After finance approves a correction, the service runs the record through matching again.
slides.question: Where does human judgment enter?
slides.reason: Show how finance corrects a record and sends it through matching again.
slides.transition: Show the record finance uses for that correction.

blocks.description: Run matching again after finance corrects a record.

slides.title: Show finance what needs correcting
slides.lead: The held record identifies the conflicting values, the reviewer and any previous correction.
slides.question: What does the reviewer need to act?
slides.reason: Show the values and history finance needs to resolve the held record.
slides.transition: Locate the held record within the proposed service.

blocks.title: Held item EX-017
blocks.description: Proposed fields for a held record.

fields.label: Conflict
fields.why: Show both values; do not guess.

fields.label: Correction
fields.why: Keep the item held until resolved.

fields.label: Replay history
fields.why: Keep the original reason when the record runs again.

slides.title: The service matches billing exports and sends approved postings
slides.lead: Billing configuration and historical migration are outside the proposed work.
slides.question: Which work and interfaces belong to this engagement?
slides.reason: Show which records enter the service and which requests leave it.
slides.transition: Use that scope to choose the tests.

blocks.description: The service reads billing exports and exchanges posting requests and receipts with the ledger.

slides.title: Test lost responses and duplicate batches before going live
slides.lead: Check that retries do not create duplicate entries and that finance can correct held records.
slides.question: What evidence would count as a pass?
slides.reason: Give each test an expected result and a record to save.
slides.transition: Explain how to stop posting after the service goes live.

rows: Posting IDs before and after replay.
Find the original receipt. Keep the request on hold if its result is unknown.
Request ID and ledger lookup response.
Keep the record on hold for finance.
Correction linked to the record of its rerun.

slides.title: Stop new postings, then check requests already sent
slides.lead: Before switching to manual processing, find out which requests the ledger accepted.
slides.question: What makes the stop path recoverable?
slides.reason: Resolve requests already sent before manual processing begins.
slides.transition: Finish with the assignments needed to start testing.

blocks.description: The operating instructions must name who can stop posting and what must be checked before it resumes.

slides.title: Assign the test preparation before approving the sandbox work
slides.question: What must be decided and assigned next?
slides.reason: Assign access, sample data, API checks and test review before the work starts.
slides.transition: The reference slides retain the detailed operating requirements.

Supply the sample and expected totals.
Check request IDs and receipt lookup.
Name who reviews the results and what counts as a pass.

slides.implication: Decide whether to allow production posting after reviewing the test results.

slides.title: Reference: keep the original batch and each correction

Notify finance when a batch stalls or held items remain.

Approve the correction and record the reason.

The team compares a complete sample with expected totals and runs the failure tests.
The controller reviews the test results and decides whether to go live.
